extension.summary: Watch Twitch streams and chat from Kodi
extension.description: View Twitch streams using Kodi's own playback, with a paired IRC chat view. Not designed for chatting back to streamers - a second way to consume streamer-generated content.
extension.news: v0.28.1: Fixed Clip playback - every clip failed with "Couldn't start playback" (silently, no log line). Twitch dropped the old thumbnail-URL-to-MP4 naming trick clips relied on (clip thumbnails moved to a new CDN path with no derivable video-file name - confirmed live). Clips now resolve their playable URL via Twitch's GQL VideoAccessToken_Clip query instead. v0.28.0: Removed the live-notify (followed-streamer "went live" notifications) feature. Live-tested extensively across v0.27.1-0.27.6: even with proactive rate-limit throttling, the cold-start subscribe burst for a large followed-channel list still overran Twitch's per-client_id EventSub rate limit and, worse, could get Twitch to close the WebSocket session outright - not worth the complexity or the risk of breaking chat for a non-essential feature. v0.27.6: Live-notify's subscribe loop now watches Ratelimit-Remaining on every SUCCESSFUL response too, not just 429s - once the budget gets low it waits for the bucket to refill before the next call, instead of only reacting after a 429 already happened. Confirmed live: even with v0.27.5's race fix, a clean cold-start 140-channel burst still 429'd on ~126 calls partway through, because the burst outran the bucket before any failure could trigger the existing reactive backoff. v0.27.5: Fixed a startup race where live-notify's service called connect() before set_broadcasters() - the background thread could snapshot an empty broadcaster set and silently defer the real subscribe burst to run ~70s late via a catchup path, colliding with chat's own EventSub subscribe if a stream was opened in the meantime (confirmed live: the "subscribed to N channels" log had already fired before any subscription request was actually made). Now set_broadcasters() is called before connect(), and the first connect attempt after Kodi boot waits 30s before starting, giving a stream opened right at boot a better chance of not colliding with the burst. v0.27.4: Live-notify's subscribe throttle now respects Twitch's own Ratelimit-Reset header on a 429 instead of a fixed 0.1s delay - confirmed live that the fixed delay wasn't enough once chat's own EventSub subscription competed for the same shared per-app rate-limit budget. v0.27.3: Fixed the SAME crash the v0.27.2 fix missed - the variable-height chat overlay (on by default for EventSub chat) has its own separate rendering code that crashed on connection-error events the same way the plain overlay used to. Confirmed live: this is what was actually crashing on kodi.local, not the file v0.27.2 patched. v0.27.2: Chat overlay no longer silently freezes if its background thread hits an unexpected error (e.g. a malformed event) - now shows a "[CHAT ERROR]" message in the chat list itself instead of only logging to kodi.log where nobody sees it. v0.27.1: Live-notify no longer subscribes your whole followed-channel list in one unthrottled burst - each subscription request is now spaced out, so a large follow list can't exhaust Twitch's shared per-app rate limit and 429 other features using the same connection (confirmed live: this was breaking chat). v0.27.0: New "VODs & Clips" screen (Twitch only) - reachable from the main menu, pick any followed channel and browse its past broadcasts and clips. Playback is video-only (no chat overlay, no ad-skip relay). v0.26.3: Renamed the addon's display name from "Twitch Center" to "SIGMA Streaming Hub" (internal addon id, script.twitch.center, is unchanged - no reinstall needed, this just updates what Kodi shows). v0.26.2: Live-go notifications now also cover streamers who were already live before the background service connected (e.g. at Kodi startup, or right after you enable the setting) - EventSub only reports the transition to live, so this adds a one-off check against currently-live followed channels immediately after connecting. v0.26.1: Live-go notification service now logs its subscribed followed-channel list and each notification it shows, plus the connect/disconnect and subscription-error diagnostics that were previously only visible with Kodi debug logging on - all gated behind a new "Log live-notify activity" setting (off by default) so it doesn't add log noise unless you turn it on. v0.26.0: Added an opt-in background notification for followed Twitch channels going live - enable "Notify when followed streamers go live" in Settings. Runs as a new Kodi background service (separate from the existing on-demand addon window), using one EventSub WebSocket subscribed to your followed channels' stream.online events. Off by default. Twitch only for now. v0.21.0: First step of Kick.com support (not usable yet - no UI wires it up): added OAuth 2.1 PKCE login, a Kick Public API client, and stream URL resolution as an internal lib/kick/ package, alongside four new hidden/advanced Settings entries (Kick Client ID, Client Secret, OAuth redirect port, saved token) for a future release to use. Kick login and browsing will follow in later updates. v0.20.0: Removed the "standalone chat window" and "both" chat display modes - neither did anything beyond what "overlay" already does ("standalone" was never implemented past a stub, "both" behaved identically to "overlay"). The "Chat display mode" setting is now a single "Show chat overlay while playing" toggle, defaulting on. If you had "standalone" selected (previously no chat during playback), you'll now see the chat overlay by default - turn the new toggle off in Settings if you don't want that. v0.19.0: Version number and release date now shown in the top-left corner of the main window, on every screen. v0.18.0: Variable-size chat overlay is now on by default for EventSub chat (still off for IRC chat, unchanged). Also fixed two bugs found during review: VariableChatOverlay's 9-line message cap wasn't actually being applied (could produce oversized message blocks for very long messages), and playback could silently fail to start at all if chat-overlay setup threw partway through - both now fixed, with a fallback so the stream always plays. v0.17.3: Live re-test of v0.17.2 found the remaining garbling wasn't a sizing issue at all - it always appeared at whatever message currently sat at the column's top edge, with content bleeding in from an already-evicted message. Root cause: a burst of messages arriving in one throttled tick could get a control added and then immediately removed again within that same call (build-then-evict-same-tick), and Kodi's addControl() appears to complete asynchronously on at least one tested build, so the same-tick removal could run before the add had actually taken effect - leaving an orphaned control behind. Restructured chat rendering to compute eviction before creating any new controls, so a message that would be evicted immediately is now never materialized as a control at all. v0.17.2: Live re-test of v0.17.1's fix on kodi.local found the overlap was reduced but not eliminated - a remaining ~1-line-tall graze specifically at block-to-block boundaries (previous message's last line vs the next message's username), not within a message's own wrapped lines. Increased _BLOCK_MARGIN (10px -> 34px), the constant meant to absorb exactly this kind of gap, and re-verified live. v0.17.1: Fixed the new variable-size chat overlay (v0.17.0) rendering with overlapping, garbled text on some Kodi builds/platforms - live testing found real text rendering taller than expected on at least one device, and because each message's position is computed from the height of the messages above it, that error compounded across the handful of messages on screen at once. Padded the per-line/per-row height constants with a large safety margin to absorb this kind of cross-build variance. v0.17.0: New "Variable-size chat overlay" setting (Settings > General, EventSub only) - sizes each chat overlay message's box to its actual length instead of always reserving space for the maximum 5-line message. Off by default; the existing fixed-box overlay stays the default for both chat engines. v0.16.5: Chat overlay message box was too short for the 5-line message cap - a 4th or 5th wrapped line spilled past the label's bottom edge into the emote-icon row below it. Grew the message box and pushed the per-item row layout (and emote icons) down to fit all 5 lines cleanly. v0.16.4: Fixed chat overlay message text still rendering with a blank line above it on some Kodi builds even after v0.16.3 - the message label had no explicit vertical alignment, so a short single-line message could render bottom/center-anchored in its box on those builds. Now pinned to the top of the box explicitly. v0.16.3: Fixed chat overlay messages sometimes rendering with a stray blank line above the text - the skin's wrapmultiline flag conflicted with the code's own manual line-wrapping. v0.16.0: New "Chat engine" setting (Settings > General) - choose between the existing anonymous IRC chat (default, no login needed) and Twitch's officially-supported EventSub chat API (requires login; available on Live Streams and Discover tabs only). EventSub falls back to IRC automatically if the channel's id can't be resolved. If the EventSub subscription itself fails (e.g. a saved login predates this version's chat scope), chat stays empty and keeps retrying - use the "Log in again" menu entry to refresh your login. Search results don't support EventSub (unauthenticated feature) - chat won't be shown when EventSub is selected for Search playback. v0.15.2: Fixed chat overlay messages getting cut off mid-word - long messages now wrap across lines instead of being cut off at the label's width. v0.15.1: No functional change - re-deploy marker for kodi.local install. v0.15.0: New landing Menu screen for navigating between Live Streams, Discover, and Search. Rebuilt the whole UI on a single persistent window with toggle-able view groups instead of constructing a new Kodi window per screen - this eliminates the Kodi window-activation revert bug for good (Discover, Search, and re-login all previously could hit it; now structurally impossible, not just less likely). v0.14.1: Fixed Search crashing on open (AttributeError in onInit) - the window would flash open then immediately bounce back to Home. Known issue: even fixed, Search can still hit the pre-existing Kodi window-activation revert bug in some cases, same as Discover/re-login - tracked separately. v0.14.0: Added an addon icon - shows in Kodi's addon browser and Add-ons list instead of the generic script placeholder. v0.13.1: Updated window tests to match the new quit-confirmation behavior introduced in v0.13.0. v0.13.0: Added a quit confirmation prompt when exiting the addon to prevent accidental closures. v0.12.0: "Log in again" on Home is now always visible (was error-only) - use it to re-authorize/switch accounts on demand, e.g. after using the same account on two devices. Website Token field is no longer masked in Settings. Shortened the Website Token help text so it renders fully on TV displays instead of getting clipped. Known issue: re-login from Home can hit a pre-existing Kodi window-activation bug and silently stay on Home instead of opening the login screen - tracked separately, not new in this release. v0.11.1: Fixed the Website Token setting (for ad-free/subscriber-perk playback) never appearing in Settings > General - an empty default value made Kodi silently drop it from the settings dialog. Also fixed the same bug for an internal setting. Both now show up and work correctly. v0.11.0: New optional "Show offline channels on Home" setting (Settings > General, off by default) - turn it on to bring offline followed channels back into Home's list, after the live ones. v0.10.0: Chat now shows automatically as a right-side overlay while a stream plays (Settings > General > Chat display mode, "overlay" or "both"). Connects anonymously to Twitch IRC, auto-reconnects on drops, and closes itself when the stream stops, ends, or errors out. Standalone full-screen chat and the picture-in-picture windowed-video layout are still to come. v0.9.0: Fixed window flicker and revert bug when opening Discover screen by adding a safe control delay and using xbmc.sleep(). Improved error handling for missing UI controls across Home and Discover windows. v0.8.1: Fixed the real cause of "stuck on login/gets a new code every time" - Home's skin defaultcontrol targeted the (empty until data loads) channel list, which made Kodi's window manager silently abort activating Home and revert to Login whenever Home wasn't the very first window shown in a session. No script-side fix could catch this since it happens before Python even runs. Same root cause and fix as Discover's earlier "flashes then reverts" bug. v0.8.0: Discover's search can now search by game/category, not just channel name - a toggle button next to the search box switches modes ("Searching: Channels" / "Searching: Games"). Searching a game (e.g. "warships") finds the best-matching category and lists its live streams. v0.7.2: Fixed streams continuing to play in the background after pressing Back - Kodi's own fullscreen-video Back only exits the fullscreen view, it doesn't stop playback. Home and Discover's Back now stop an active stream instead of closing the whole addon out from under it. v0.7.1: Added a Settings button on Home - opens Kodi's native addon settings dialog directly (no more digging through Add-ons browser context menus), and reloads Home afterward so a newly pasted Website Token takes effect immediately. v0.7.0: New optional "Website Token" setting (Settings > General) - paste your twitch.tv browser session's auth-token cookie to unlock ad-free/subscriber-perk playback and get the followed-games filter row actually working (it silently 401'd before, same root cause as the playback bug). Leave it empty to keep the default anonymous/public behavior. v0.6.5: Fixed playback always failing with "session expired": Twitch's internal GraphQL API permanently rejects any real user OAuth token from a non-Twitch client_id, so no refresh could ever fix it. Playback token requests are now made anonymously, which Twitch serves fine for public live streams. v0.6.4: Fixed Login screen restarting the device-code flow (new code shown) after a successful login, when Kodi re-fires the window's init on an already-completed login. v0.6.3: Token refresh failures are now logged with the actual reason (network error, HTTP status, bad response body) instead of silently forcing a re-login with no diagnostic trail. v0.6.2: Fixed Home's focus landing on a random button (Relogin/Discover) right after load - the skin's defaultcontrol targeted the channel list before it had items, so Kodi's focus fallback could pick a button; a stray keypress there would silently trigger unwanted navigation. v0.6.1: Fixed login screen ending the whole script on successful login instead of continuing to Home - required reopening the addon manually every time the session expired. v0.6.0: Real stream playback via inputstream.adaptive; clicking a live channel in Home or Discover now plays it. v0.5.0: Discover screen (browse by game, channel search); fixed window navigation killing the script; fixed unreachable skin controls. v0.4.0: followed-games filter row on Home. v0.3.0: Home screen (followed channels, thumbnails, token refresh). v0.2.0: Twitch device-code login. v0.1.0: initial addon scaffold.

extension.summary: Jellyfin client with a Plex-style interface
extension.description: Connects to a Jellyfin media server and presents a custom, hub-based home screen, poster-wall browsing, and item detail pages modelled on the Plex Web/App interface, instead of Kodi's default skin listings.
Install this once to let Kodi automatically discover and install updates for Twitch Center and Jellyfin (Plex-style).
